decisions.question: scope (small vs proposal), hook point, list strategy, risks

risks: Name collision: a user-defined returning global function whose stripped/namespace-guarded name matches a listed token (e.g. a local `exit`/`panic`) would be wrongly treated as noreturn -- mitigated by the upstream global/std namespace guard; identical risk profile to the already-default-on noreturn_known, which name-matches the same list.

Flow-query-only sets only the flow-time artificialHalt, not the FunctionSymbol proto's is_no_return flag; flow.rs ORs the env query at the exact dead-flow-drop site and inserts the same halt, matching the documented W4-era seam pattern; output matches the proven `option noreturn` path.
ET_REL-only relevance: real-ELF/PLT callees resolve via the address-keyed noreturn scan already, so default-ON is a no-op there; the 0/675 ablation confirms no real-ELF datatest regresses.
decision.justification: Verified against the code: query_call_no_return is the exact seam (flow.rs ORs it with the proto flag at the artificialHalt/dead-flow-drop site), function_display_name_across_scopes sits adjacent so name resolution is trivial, and the vendored list is ~20 entries with a documented leading-`_`-strip convention. 2 ported-core anchor files + 1 new module + registry boilerplate; no new pass type, no S7, under the proposal-gate thresholds. Full include_str! list reuses the single vendored source of truth at zero crate-dependency cost. Keep default-OFF pending the 0/675 ablation given the name-collision risk.

decisions.question: default-ON vs opt-in after the ablation
decisions.decision: Ship default-ON (DIV-13; renumbered from DIV-12 on merge after PR #90 took DIV-12 for the region structurer). The ablation is clean (0/675 upstream + stage assertions unchanged at the default), the feature is 23% faster on the target, it is a correctness fix, and it adds no risk class beyond the already-default-on noreturn_known (same vendored list, same namespace guard). Recorded interaction: `option noreturn_known off` alone no longer restores the post-`exit` dead code; the PE multiformat test now disables both name-based gates.
